- Avoid over-optimism in early forecast periods; model tends to overestimate prices in the first few days after a spike.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices; adjust downward by 1–2% for the first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >70.00), model often overshoots in the immediate 3–5 day window; apply a 1–3% downward correction to prevent overreaction.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day forecasts: model frequently fails to capture the 10–15 day pullback after a peak; add a 0.5–1.5% downward bias in the 10–15 day horizon.
- If sentiment remains flat, model should not assume momentum; instead, treat 30-day forecasts as “no trend” and apply a conservative, symmetric correction around recent 14-day average.
- Avoid forecasting upward trends after a 30-day low; model often misinterprets low prices as “bottom” and overreacts; cap upward forecasts at +1.5% above recent 14-day low.
